action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies show the upper-limb motor involvement with absent F-waves and normal legs that defines the variant, and repetitive stimulation of facial, accessory and limb nerves tests for a neuromuscular transmission defect [EAN_PNS_2023, Wakerley_2014].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Albuminocytological dissociation: raised protein with cells <5/mm3 (5-50/mm3 compatible but prompts an alternative; >50/mm3 suggests another diagnosis); protein may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein and glucose
action_criteria.rationale: CSF albuminocytological dissociation supports GBS, and normal cell count and cytology argue against leptomeningeal malignancy and infection [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No acute infarct or brainstem lesion; lower cranial nerve enhancement may be seen
action_criteria.label: Brain MRI with brainstem and skull-base imaging
action_criteria.rationale: Bulbar weakness in a woman with a prior stroke needs brainstem imaging to exclude a new infarct, a brainstem lesion or a skull-base process.

action_criteria.label: Acetylcholine receptor and MuSK antibodies
action_criteria.rationale: Bulbar and neck weakness is the typical presentation of myasthenia gravis, the main mimic of this variant; antibodies with repetitive stimulation test for it.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Anti-GT1a IgG positive (1:160), anti-GQ1b negative: supports the PCB variant without Miller Fisher overlap; a send-out result that does not delay treatment
action_criteria.label: Serum anti-GT1a IgG (with anti-GQ1b) for the pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant
action_criteria.rationale: Anti-GT1a IgG, often with anti-GQ1b, is the antibody of the pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant (Wakerley 2014); anti-GQ1b on the same request looks for a Miller Fisher overlap. EAN/PNS 2023 restricts ganglioside testing to the MFS spectrum and its regional variants.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Botulinum neurotoxin not detected in serum
action_criteria.label: Optional serum botulinum toxin assay for the descending bulbar mimic
action_criteria.rationale: Botulism is the descending bulbar mimic of the PCB variant; normal pupils and eye movements, areflexia in the weak arms, raised CSF protein and no food, wound or injection exposure already make it very unlikely, so the reference-laboratory assay is optional.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Baseline values before treatment; abnormal liver tests or low albumin mark a higher risk of a severe course; no metabolic or toxic alternative
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose and CK
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests exclude metabolic mimics and give the baseline before IVIg; low albumin carries prognostic weight [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Bulbar weakness with a weak cough and silent aspiration is the main threat; serial FVC, MIP and MEP with cough and secretion assessment set the level of monitoring [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: normal sinus rhythm 68-96 bpm and blood pressure 124/72 to 146/86 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction is common in GBS and can cause bradyarrhythmias, pauses and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 88, with normal PR, QRS and QTc (434 ms) as the baseline
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline 12-lead ECG screens for autonomic rhythm and conduction changes and gives the QTc before treatment [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.label: Optional single-fibre EMG for seronegative myasthenia
action_criteria.rationale: Single-fibre EMG is the most sensitive test for a neuromuscular transmission defect when antibodies and repetitive stimulation are negative.

action_criteria.label: Optional nodal and paranodal antibodies (prior episode)
action_criteria.rationale: A previous self-limited episode raises recurrent GBS; nodal and paranodal antibodies are tested when an autoimmune nodopathy is suspected [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No interaction that changes the choice of IVIg or plasma exchange
action_criteria.label: Optional interaction check with amlodipine and aspirin before IVIg or plasma exchange
action_criteria.rationale: Amlodipine and aspirin do not interact with IVIg and aspirin does not preclude lumbar puncture, so the check cannot change management.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on the pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
Do not delay IVIg while waiting for the send-out anti-GT1a and anti-GQ1b result.
required_recommendations: Admit to ICU-level (high-dependency) monitoring because of bulbar weakness with a weak cough and silent aspiration: nil by mouth with nasogastric feeding, aspiration precautions and suction, and FVC, MIP, MEP and cough every 4-6 hours; intubate for airway protection if secretions cannot be cleared or aspiration recurs, or if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg (about 1.4 L at 70.7 kg), MIP becomes weaker than -30 cmH2O or MEP falls below 40 cmH2O [EAN_PNS_2023, Lawn_2001].

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 28 g/day at 70.7 kg) now, at the end of the 2-week window, because of progressive bulbar and neck weakness with aspiration; plasma exchange (200-250 mL/kg over 5 sessions, within 4 weeks of onset) is an equivalent alternative [EAN_PNS_2023].
Treat the right lower lobe aspiration pneumonia with antibiotics according to local guidance for aspiration pneumonia.
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses.
Speech and language therapy reassessment of swallowing before any oral intake resumes.

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.

differential.key_features: Bulbar and neck weakness fit, but there is no ptosis, ophthalmoparesis or fatigability, the weak arms are areflexic, AChR, MuSK and LRP4 antibodies are negative, 3 Hz stimulation of facial, accessory and ulnar nerves shows no decrement, and the CSF protein is raised.

Descending bulbar palsy, but pupils and eye movements are normal, there is no food, wound or injection exposure, and areflexia confined to the weak arms with raised CSF protein is not botulism; the serum botulinum toxin assay, if sent, is negative.
Prior stroke on aspirin raises it, but the deficits are lower motor neuron with arm areflexia and the MRI shows no acute infarct or brainstem lesion.
Acute 2-week course, a previous remitting episode, areflexia, no fasciculations, wasting or upper motor neuron signs, and raised CSF protein.
Weight loss of 4 kg is explained by 2 weeks of dysphagia, albumin 3.2 by poor intake and pneumonia; CT chest shows no mass or lymphadenopathy, CSF cytology is negative and CEA and CA-125 are normal.

The self-limited episode 3 years ago may have been a first GBS episode; recurrence occurs in a few percent of patients. Nodal and paranodal antibodies are negative; reassess for acute-onset CIDP if she fluctuates or progresses beyond 8 weeks.
Fully vaccinated, no pharyngitis or membrane.

key_clinical_evidence: Oropharyngeal, neck and proximal arm weakness with areflexia in the arms and normal legs defines the pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant [Wakerley_2014]; the upper-limb motor NCS with absent F-waves and CSF albuminocytological dissociation (protein 68 mg/dL, 2 cells/mm3) support it.

Absent gag and palatal reflexes do not separate GBS from myasthenia gravis; areflexia in the weak arms, raised CSF protein, absent upper-limb F-waves and normal facial, accessory and limb repetitive stimulation do.

Anti-GT1a IgG supports the variant but does not establish it on its own; it is a send-out test and does not delay treatment. Anti-GQ1b is negative and there is no ophthalmoplegia or ataxia to suggest Miller Fisher overlap.
A previous episode is a reason to consider recurrent GBS and, if the course fluctuates or progresses beyond 8 weeks, acute-onset CIDP or a nodopathy [EAN_PNS_2023].
Bulbar weakness with weak cough and silent aspiration is an indication for ICU-level monitoring even when FVC is preserved [EAN_PNS_2023].

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The deficits are lower motor neuron with areflexia in the weak arms, and the MRI shows only the old occipital infarct with no brainstem lesion.
red_herrings.data_point: Prior posterior cerebral artery stroke on aspirin
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a new brainstem stroke as the cause of the bulbar palsy.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Two weeks of severe dysphagia and an aspiration pneumonia explain the weight loss and albumin; CT chest, CSF cytology and tumour markers show no malignancy.
red_herrings.data_point: 4 kg weight loss with low albumin
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests an occult malignancy with a paraneoplastic syndrome.

interactions: Aspirin: antiplatelet effect relevant to central venous access for plasma exchange; aspirin alone is not regarded as a contraindication to lumbar puncture.
Amlodipine: additive hypotension with volume shifts during plasma exchange.
general.proposed: IVIg or plasma exchange, lumbar puncture; current medicines amlodipine, aspirin
general.summary: No interaction that changes the choice between IVIg and plasma exchange; category-level cautions only.
warnings: No interaction identified between IVIg and amlodipine or aspirin.

ecg.interpretation: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal PR, QRS, and QTc intervals.

labs.interpretation: Leukocytosis (WBC 12.8). Albumin 3.2 g/dL (low). Remaining values within reference ranges.

results.finding: The pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant presents with oropharyngeal, neck and proximal arm weakness with arm areflexia and relative sparing of the legs; incomplete forms include isolated acute pharyngeal weakness; anti-GT1a IgG is found in a proportion of patients.

IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided and should be considered in ambulant patients with rapid progression or bulbar, autonomic or respiratory involvement; corticosteroids are not advised.

general.summary: The pharyngeal-cervical-brachial variant is a localised GBS form defined clinically; bulbar involvement is a reason to consider IVIg or plasma exchange even in ambulant patients [Wakerley_2014, EAN_PNS_2023].

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL study. 1. Reduced median and ulnar CMAP amplitudes with normal distal latencies and conduction velocities, and absent upper-limb F-waves. 2. Normal lower-limb motor and all sensory studies. 3. No decrement on 3 Hz repetitive stimulation of facial, spinal accessory and ulnar nerves. 4. Reduced recruitment with scattered fibrillation potentials in proximal arm muscles. Findings indicate a motor neuropathy or radiculopathy affecting the upper limbs, without a neuromuscular transmission defect. Clinical correlation recommended.

quantitative_data.pattern: Motor neuropathy confined to the upper limbs with absent upper-limb F-waves; normal RNS

metadata.difficulty_description: Pharyngeal-cervical-brachial GBS in a 74-year-old: bulbar, neck and arm weakness with arm areflexia and normal legs; myasthenia gravis, brainstem stroke, botulism and malignancy must be excluded; anti-GT1a is a send-out result.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required actions (NCS/EMG, CSF, baseline labs, respiratory function, telemetry) plus recommended brain MRI and myasthenia antibodies; 2 red herrings (prior stroke, weight loss).
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Two weeks of progressive difficulty swallowing with hoarseness and aspiration, and for one week difficulty holding up her head and lifting her arms.

past_medical_history: Prior left posterior cerebral artery infarction 9 years ago (no residual deficits)

patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. L. is a 74-year-old retired librarian with a 2-week history of progressive dysphagia. It began with difficulty swallowing during meals, then frequent coughing on liquids and solids and nasal regurgitation, with a hoarse voice. Over the past week she has also had difficulty holding up her head and lifting her arms to brush her hair; her legs feel normal and she walks without difficulty. She has lost 4 kg because she cannot eat adequately. Three years ago she had a transient episode of difficulty swallowing that resolved spontaneously within weeks without a diagnosis. She reports no infection or vaccination in the preceding weeks, no diplopia, ptosis, facial weakness, sensory symptoms, fatigable or fluctuating weakness, and no home-canned food, wounds or injection drug use. She is fully vaccinated, including against diphtheria. Before referral, flexible laryngoscopy showed normal vocal cord movement with pooling of secretions; a videofluoroscopic swallow study showed severe oropharyngeal dysphagia with silent aspiration; contrast CT of the neck showed no structural obstruction; and CT chest showed right lower lobe consolidation consistent with aspiration, with no mass or lymphadenopathy. A nasogastric tube was placed for feeding.

neurological_exam.additional: Nasogastric tube in place. Prior left posterior cerebral artery infarct 9 years ago without residual deficit.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose limited by arm weakness without dysmetria; heel-shin intact.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Gag reflex absent bilaterally. Palatal elevation reduced bilaterally. Hoarse, weak voice; coughs on sips of water; weak cough. Tongue strength normal, no tongue wasting or fasciculations. No facial weakness, no ptosis, full eye movements without fatigable weakness or diplopia. Pupils equal and reactive.
neurological_exam.motor: Neck flexion 3/5, neck extension 4/5. Shoulder abduction 4/5, elbow flexion 4/5, elbow extension 4+/5, grip 4+/5 bilaterally. Lower limbs 5/5 throughout. No fasciculations; tone normal. No fatigability on sustained upgaze or repeated arm abduction.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps, triceps and brachioradialis absent bilaterally. Knee 2+ and ankle 1+ bilaterally. Plantars flexor. No jaw jerk.
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch, pinprick, vibration and joint position in all limbs.

physical_exam.general: Weight 70.7 kg (74.7 kg two weeks ago), height 160 cm. Coarse crackles at the right lung base. Pharynx without membrane or exudate.
